title: manifest.json
description: An inventory of a review bundle, written last. docs/05-file-contracts.md lists the file but never shows its contents; this schema is a W0-B design decision. It answers the three questions a watcher on the other side has: is this bundle complete, has it changed since I last looked, and what wrote it. The bundle is assembled in a sibling .tmp directory and renamed into place, so a watcher should never see a partial bundle — the manifest covers the case a rename cannot, such as a bundle copied or synced file by file.

documentId.description: The reviewed document's meta.json id, verbatim.

reviewFolder.description: The bundle's own directory name, <slug>.review, so a manifest copied elsewhere still says where it belongs.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601, when the bundle was written.

files.description: Every file in the bundle except manifest.json itself, which cannot list its own hash. Sorted by path.

complete.description: Whether the bundle is finished. Always true in a manifest this app writes, since the manifest is written last. Optional: a watcher treats its absence as complete, and only an explicit false means wait.

origin.description: The reviewed document's origin, copied verbatim from its meta.json so the bundle carries its own return path. A watcher reads this before falling back to inbox/<slug>/meta.json, which only resolves while that folder still has the name the bundle expects. Same shape as meta.json's origin block; every field is optional there and every field is optional here.

name.description: pencil-in-the-loop for bundles this app writes. Another value means another tool wrote a compatible bundle, which is allowed and is rather the point.

path.description: Bundle-relative, forward slashes, no leading slash: review.md, ink/page-01.png.

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the file's contents. Lets a watcher tell a re-sent bundle from a re-synced one.
